newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese bonds sharply down on EMU, rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese bonds sharply down on EMU, rate fears.

text.p: Portuguese bonds sank in nervous trade amid fears over the timing of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) and a possible U.S. rate rise, and could fall further tomorrow, dealers said.
"The market closed at the lows and is still on the selling side. The June 1997 future has room to fall further in line with Bonos," said a fixed rate director.
He added: "Portuguese 10-year bonds could fall further as spreads against Bonos are very high."
Another said: "The market is very nervous, both because of EMU and the possibility of a U.S. rate rise."
